protocol.topic:
Network meta-analysis of radiotherapy modalities for choroidal (and broader uveal) melanoma.

Research question:
Among patients with uveal melanoma (choroidal-predominant cohorts plus mixed
uveal melanoma cohorts under the uveal-relaxed restart), how do I-125 plaque
brachytherapy, Ru-106 plaque brachytherapy, proton beam therapy, carbon ion
therapy, and photon stereotactic radiotherapy or fractionated stereotactic
radiotherapy compare for local control / local recurrence pooled at 1, 3, 5,
and 10 years (with follow-up year fit as a continuous meta-regression
covariate), survival endpoints at the same time-points, eye retention,
visual acuity loss, and major radiation-related complications?

Outcome reconciliation note:
The earlier R scripts in the submission package implemented a single 5-year
local-control snapshot; this restriction has been superseded. The primary
endpoint family is now multi-time-point (1, 3, 5, 10 years), and follow-up
year is fit as a continuous mixed-effects meta-regression covariate per
modality and across the connected network. The 5-year value anchors the main
NMA league table and SUCRA ranking; the 1/3/10-year values support
transitivity inspection and a dose–time–effect surface comparable across
modalities. Survival endpoints are separated and labeled exactly as reported
(melanoma-specific survival, overall survival, metastasis-free survival)
rather than merged. Population breadth is set to be at least as inclusive as
Tseng YH 2024 (Eye, charged-particle vs brachytherapy SR/MA in uveal melanoma).

Current reconstruction source:
This project is being reconstructed from an existing Green Journal submission
package located at:

/Users/wangtingwei/Desktop/choroidal_melanoma_NMA_publication_package

The available local package includes the extracted study-level CSV, final R
analysis scripts, generated results, figures, manuscript, supplement, PRISMA
checklist, and submission documents. Earlier pipeline artifacts such as
original protocol, database search logs, deduplication records, screening
decisions, and full-text retrieval manifest are not present in the package and
must be reconstructed or marked as unavailable in later stages.

studies_head.title: Uveal melanoma: Treatment approaches and prognostic outcomes based on the American joint committee on cancer staging
studies_head.setting: Ramathibodi Hospital tertiary ocular oncology center
studies_head.followup_summary: Median 37.3 months, range 1-130
studies_head.diagnosis_basis: Clinical and histopathologic where enucleated
studies_head.pico_population_status: Choroidal-dominant mixed uveal above 85 percent threshold
studies_head.eligibility_note: Eligible for extraction as mixed uveal cohort with 94.3 percent choroidal disease; age range includes 16, so keep age caveat.

studies_head.title: Endoresection in Choroidal Melanoma: Outcomes of Intentional Incomplete Tumor Removal
studies_head.setting: Bellvitge University Hospital single tertiary ocular oncology center
studies_head.followup_summary: Mean 41.70 months, SD 17.98; median 38 months, IQR 27, range 11-75
studies_head.diagnosis_basis: Clinical with intraoperative histopathologic/cytogenetic tumor sampling
studies_head.eligibility_note: Eligible for descriptive extraction; combined endoresection plus adjuvant Ru-106 is not a direct primary radiotherapy node.

studies_head.title: Carbon Ion Versus Photon-based Stereotactic Ablative Radiation Therapy for Patients with Choroidal Melanoma
studies_head.setting: QST Hospital carbon ion center in Japan and Gangnam Severance/Yonsei tertiary hospital in South Korea
studies_head.design: Retrospective comparative cohort with propensity score matching
studies_head.age_summary: Before PSM median age 56.0 years in CIRT and 60.0 years in SABR; after PSM median age 60.0 years in both arms
studies_head.followup_summary: Median follow-up 70.2 months for CIRT and 51.9 months for SABR
studies_head.diagnosis_basis: Clinical and imaging-based diagnosis of localized choroidal melanoma
studies_head.eligibility_note: Eligible comparative radiotherapy extraction; primary numeric outcomes are from the propensity score-matched cohort unless otherwise noted.

studies_head.title: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes for Adolescent and Young-Adult Uveal Melanoma Patients Treated with Dedicated Particle-Beam Radiation
studies_head.setting: University of California San Francisco dedicated ocular particle-beam program
studies_head.design: Retrospective cohort from prospectively maintained institutional database
studies_head.age_summary: PBRT median age 38.3 years, range 13.3-45.9; helium median age 37.1 years, range 18.1-45.5
studies_head.followup_summary: PBRT median follow-up 85.7 months, range 3-301; helium median follow-up 256.7 months, range 24-450
studies_head.diagnosis_basis: Clinical uveal melanoma evaluation with FNA biopsy in subset
studies_head.pico_population_status: Choroidal-dominant mixed uveal above 85 percent threshold for PBRT; helium choroidal proportion not directly reported
studies_head.eligibility_note: Extract PBRT as choroidal-dominant particle-beam evidence; helium ion is contextual/sensitivity-only outside current 5-node network.

studies_head.title: Threshold analysis of mortality outcomes in the collaborative ocular melanoma study (COMS)
studies_head.setting: Collaborative Ocular Melanoma Study multicenter trial data reanalyzed by Karolinska/St Erik investigators
studies_head.design: Threshold analysis of public randomized trial results
studies_head.followup_summary: 12-year melanoma mortality data from COMS public results
studies_head.diagnosis_basis: COMS medium choroidal melanoma trial eligibility
studies_head.eligibility_note: Contextual reanalysis of COMS mortality; PDF does not provide new extractable 5-year local-control or eye-retention outcomes.

studies_head.title: Characteristics and Outcomes of 237 Juxtapapillary Choroidal Melanomas Treated with Iodine-125 Plaque Brachytherapy
studies_head.setting: University of Tennessee Health Science Center single institution
studies_head.age_summary: Age at surgery mean 61 years, SD 14; median 62
studies_head.followup_summary: Follow-up mean 5.3 years, SD 4.6; median 4.1 years
studies_head.diagnosis_basis: Clinical diagnosis of juxtapapillary choroidal melanoma
studies_head.eligibility_note: Eligible I-125 plaque cohort; juxtapapillary anatomy should be retained as high-risk tumor-size/location context.

studies_head.title: Clinical outcomes and risk factors for local failure and visual impairment in patients treated with Ru-106 brachytherapy for uveal melanoma

# Abstract

## Background

Radiotherapy options for choroidal melanoma include iodine-125 plaque brachytherapy, ruthenium-106 plaque brachytherapy, proton beam therapy, carbon-ion radiotherapy, and photon stereotactic or fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy. Published evidence is dominated by non-randomized cohorts and single-arm case series, making direct comparative synthesis difficult.

## Objective

To synthesize 5-year clinical outcomes after radiotherapy for choroidal melanoma using corrected full-text extraction and arm-based proportional meta-analysis.

## Methods

We included adult choroidal melanoma cohorts treated with iodine-125 plaque, ruthenium-106 plaque, proton beam therapy, carbon-ion radiotherapy, or photon stereotactic/fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy. Mixed uveal melanoma cohorts were eligible when choroidal disease represented at least 85% of the cohort. Eligible study designs included randomized trials, non-randomized comparative studies, and case series with at least 20 patients and sufficient follow-up for actuarial or Kaplan-Meier estimates around 5 years. Corrected full texts were extracted into study, arm, and outcome tables. Local recurrence estimates were converted to local-control success for analysis only. Proportions were pooled by treatment node using random-effects logit-transformed proportional meta-analysis. Network meta-analysis was not performed because corrected extraction did not yield a connected comparative evidence network.

## Results

The active full-text screening set contained 1,565 records, of which 85 were included for extraction. The corrected extraction contained 85 studies, 128 treatment arms, and 573 outcome rows; 218 quantitative rows were analysis-ready after duplicate and endpoint cleanup. For 5-year local control, pooled estimates were highest for proton beam therapy (95.29% (90.87% to 97.63%)) and carbon-ion radiotherapy (94.14% (91.54% to 95.98%)), followed by photon SRS/FSRT (91.47% (84.26% to 95.55%)), iodine-125 plaque (90.74% (87.34% to 93.3%)), and ruthenium-106 plaque (80.81% (75.69% to 85.07%)). Five-year eye-retention estimates were 92.31% (89.42% to 94.45%) for carbon-ion radiotherapy, 87.38% (84.87% to 89.53%) for iodine-125 plaque, 86.85% (71.18% to 94.65%) for ruthenium-106 plaque, 85.44% (74.55% to 92.16%) for proton beam therapy, and 79.75% (74.21% to 84.35%) for photon SRS/FSRT. Survival endpoints were analyzed separately as overall, disease-specific, melanoma-specific, and metastasis-free survival rather than pooled across definitions. The corrected comparative primary-outcome evidence contained 1 comparative study and 2 arms, insufficient for a connected 5-node network meta-analysis.

## Conclusions

Corrected full-text synthesis supports arm-based pooled outcome estimates by radiotherapy modality, but not a defensible network meta-analysis. Cross-modality differences should be interpreted descriptively because arm-based estimates remain vulnerable to confounding by tumor size, treatment era, center experience, selection criteria, and outcome definitions.

Five-year eye-retention estimates were 92.31% (89.42% to 94.45%) for carbon-ion radiotherapy, 87.38% (84.87% to 89.53%) for iodine-125 plaque, 86.85% (71.18% to 94.65%) for ruthenium-106 plaque, 85.44% (74.55% to 92.16%) for proton beam therapy, and 79.75% (74.21% to 84.35%) for photon SRS/FSRT. # Introduction

Choroidal melanoma is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults. Local treatment aims to control tumor growth, preserve the globe when clinically appropriate, and minimize treatment-related visual morbidity while maintaining survival outcomes. Contemporary management includes plaque brachytherapy with iodine-125 or ruthenium-106, proton beam therapy, carbon-ion radiotherapy, and photon-based stereotactic or fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy.

Comparative interpretation across modalities is difficult because treatment selection is strongly influenced by tumor size, location, proximity to the optic disc or fovea, era of treatment, institutional expertise, and eligibility for eye-preserving therapy. Although network meta-analysis is attractive in principle, a valid network requires traceable within-study comparative contrasts and a connected treatment graph. After corrected full-text extraction, the available comparative evidence did not support such a network. We therefore performed an arm-based proportional meta-analysis and treated cross-modality comparisons as descriptive rather than causal.

# Methods

## Eligibility Criteria

We included adults with histologically or clinically diagnosed choroidal melanoma treated with iodine-125 plaque brachytherapy, ruthenium-106 plaque brachytherapy, proton beam therapy, carbon-ion radiotherapy, or photon stereotactic/fractionated stereotactic radiotherapy. COMS-era enucleation cohorts were retained as contextual survival anchors but were not used as active radiotherapy nodes. Mixed uveal melanoma cohorts were eligible only if at least 85% of patients had choroidal disease. Eligible designs were randomized trials, non-randomized comparative studies, and case series with at least 20 patients and sufficient follow-up to support actuarial or Kaplan-Meier outcomes around 5 years.

## Screening And Full-Text Verification

Records underwent title/abstract screening followed by full-text screening. Full-text decisions were grounded in the PICO criteria and corrected PDF identity checks. Wrong-content PDFs were replaced or excluded before extraction. Records without assessable correct full text were not treated as scientific exclusions.

The active full-text screening file contains 1,565 records: 85 included for extraction, 500 excluded by full-text eligibility, 578 not full-text assessed, 377 screened out before full text, and 25 duplicate or superseded.

## Data Extraction

Data were extracted into study-characteristics, arm-level, and long-format outcome tables. Extracted fields included study design, country, setting, recruitment years, treatment node, arm denominator, dose or fractionation when available, tumor-size context, outcome family, endpoint label, timepoint, event count, denominator, percentage, confidence interval, direction of benefit, and source evidence.

The corrected extraction included 85 studies, 128 arms, and 573 outcome rows. After duplicate and endpoint cleanup, 218 quantitative rows were analysis-ready.

## Outcomes

The primary outcome was 5-year local control. When studies reported local recurrence or local failure, values were converted to local-control success for analysis only. Secondary outcomes included eye retention, overall survival, disease-specific survival, melanoma-specific survival, metastasis-free survival, metastasis, visual acuity worse than 20/200, neovascular glaucoma, radiation maculopathy, cataract surgery, and radiation optic neuropathy. Survival endpoint families were not combined.

## Statistical Analysis

Arm-level proportions were pooled by treatment node using random-effects proportional meta-analysis with logit transformation, inverse-variance weighting, and restricted maximum-likelihood heterogeneity estimation. Results are reported as pooled percentages with 95% confidence intervals. Because the corrected full-text extraction contained only 1 comparative primary local-control study and 2 comparative arms across 2 treatment nodes, a connected 5-node network meta-analysis was not performed.

## Sensitivity And Subgroup Analyses

To test the robustness of the primary arm-based estimates and the conclusion that the corrected extraction does not support a connected network meta-analysis, the following pre-specified sensitivity and subgroup analyses were run. Descriptor files for each run are stored under `06_analysis/sensitivity/` and point to the underlying tables and scripts.

1. Three-node collapsed pool. The primary 5-node pool was re-estimated after collapsing iodine-125 and ruthenium-106 plaque into a single Brachytherapy node, to test whether node granularity drives modality-level point estimates (`06_analysis/run_3node_collapsed_analysis.R`).
2. Crude local-control endpoint sensitivity. The head-to-head comparative dataset was rebuilt using crude local control at last follow-up rather than 5-year actuarial / Kaplan-Meier local control, to test whether the primary-endpoint definition is what disconnects the network (`06_analysis/build_crude_local_control_sensitivity.py`).
3. Uveal-relaxed population sensitivity. Records previously excluded under the >=85% choroidal-dominance rule were re-screened against a relaxed uveal population rule, to test whether the strict population criterion materially changes the available comparative evidence.
4. Endpoint-family subgroup analysis. Survival endpoint families (overall, disease-specific, melanoma-specific, metastasis-free) and complication-specific endpoints were pooled separately by treatment node rather than merged across endpoint definitions.
5. Exploratory mixed-endpoint local-failure NMA. A reconstruction-based NMA over log-odds-ratio local-failure contrasts was run as an exploratory sensitivity only; it is not used for any manuscript ranking or treatment recommendation (`06_analysis/run_exploratory_local_control_nma.R`).

No leave-one-out per-study deletion, fixed-effects re-estimation, Egger's regression, or trim-and-fill funnel correction was performed in the primary report; the very small number of comparative arms makes these classical NMA-bias diagnostics uninformative for the present dataset.

# Results

## Study Flow And Evidence Base

The final corrected extraction set included 85 studies and 128 treatment arms. Eight wrong-PDF records identified during extraction were corrected and re-extracted. One duplicate COMS Report No. 19 record was excluded from analysis-ready tables.

## Comparative Evidence And NMA Feasibility

Corrected extraction identified only one comparative study with extractable primary 5-year local-control data: Kim 2025, comparing carbon-ion radiotherapy with photon SABR. This produced two comparative arms across two nodes and did not support a connected network. Therefore, network meta-analysis was not performed.

## Sensitivity And Subgroup Findings

The five pre-specified sensitivity and subgroup analyses described in Methods produced the following results.

1. Three-node collapsed pool. Re-pooling under three collapsed nodes gave 5-year local-control estimates of 85.23% (80.84-88.75; k=17 arms) for Brachytherapy, 95.29% (90.87-97.63; k=6) for Proton beam therapy, and 91.47% (84.26-95.55; k=4) for Photon SRS/FSRT. The qualitative ordering of modalities and the absence of a connected comparative network were unchanged from the primary 5-node analysis.
2. Crude local-control endpoint sensitivity. Relaxing the primary endpoint from 5-year actuarial / Kaplan-Meier to crude local control at last follow-up moved Jarczak 2026 from sensitivity-only into the core crude evidence pool, but the Brachytherapy-Proton-Carbon comparative network remained disconnected because the carbon-ion node is anchored only by Kim 2025, which reports 5-year Kaplan-Meier local failure rather than crude last-follow-up local control.
3. Uveal-relaxed population sensitivity. Reassessment of records excluded under the >=85% choroidal-dominance rule identified a small set of mixed-uveal studies that became analysis-ready under the relaxed rule. None of these records reconnected the primary 5-node comparative network.
4. Endpoint-family subgroup analysis. Survival endpoint families (overall, disease-specific, melanoma-specific, metastasis-free) and complication-specific endpoints (neovascular glaucoma, radiation maculopathy, radiation optic neuropathy, cataract surgery, visual acuity worse than 20/200) were pooled separately by treatment node and are reported in the manuscript tables. Heterogeneity I^2 frequently exceeded 80% within complication families, supporting the decision to report these as descriptive subgroup estimates rather than as causal modality rankings.
5. Exploratory mixed-endpoint local-failure NMA. The exploratory reconstruction NMA produced an indicative league table with wide confidence intervals (e.g. Carbon-ion vs I-125 plaque OR 0.37, 95% CI 0.15-0.94) but mixes crude and actuarial local-failure definitions. The result is reported only as a sensitivity exploration and is not used for any treatment ranking or clinical recommendation.

Taken together, the sensitivity and subgroup analyses support the primary report's two methodological claims: arm-based proportional meta-analysis is defensible for endpoint-specific modality summaries, and the corrected comparative evidence is insufficient for a connected network meta-analysis regardless of node-granularity choices, endpoint-definition relaxations, or population-criterion relaxations.

# Discussion

This corrected synthesis provides an auditable arm-based summary of 5-year outcomes after radiotherapy for choroidal melanoma. The analysis suggests high local-control rates across modern radiotherapy modalities, with pooled 5-year local control above 90% for proton beam therapy, carbon-ion radiotherapy, photon SRS/FSRT, and iodine-125 plaque brachytherapy. Ruthenium-106 plaque estimates were lower in the current extraction, with substantial heterogeneity, likely reflecting differences in tumor selection, lesion thickness, plaque geometry, treatment era, and outcome definition.

The most important methodological finding is that the corrected evidence base does not support a connected network meta-analysis. Earlier reconstruction files suggested a 5-node NMA, but those contrasts were not traceable to corrected full-text extraction and included hardcoded denominators, inferred event counts, mixed endpoint definitions, and non-comparable timepoints. The current analysis avoids those assumptions and reports only estimates supported by the corrected extraction.

Survival outcomes require particular caution. Overall survival, disease-specific survival, melanoma-specific survival, and metastasis-free survival answer different clinical questions and were therefore separated. Future comparative work should pre-specify survival endpoint hierarchy and extract time-specific actuarial estimates directly from source tables or Kaplan-Meier curves.

## Clinical Interpretation

The pooled local-control estimates support the effectiveness of radiotherapy for local tumor control, but modality selection should not be based on arm-based ranking alone. Treatment choice remains dependent on tumor size, thickness, location, visual potential, availability of proton or carbon-ion facilities, plaque suitability, and patient preference.

## Strengths

Strengths include corrected full-text verification, explicit wrong-PDF correction before extraction, source-evidence fields for extracted outcomes, endpoint-specific survival separation, duplicate cleanup, and avoidance of unsupported network meta-analysis claims.

## Limitations

Limitations include reliance on observational cohorts and case series, substantial between-study heterogeneity, variable tumor-size distributions, incomplete reporting of endpoint definitions, mixed historical and modern treatment eras, and residual confounding in arm-based comparisons. Because most included evidence is non-randomized and single-arm, the pooled proportions describe modality-specific outcomes but do not estimate causal comparative effects.

# Conclusions

Corrected full-text extraction supports arm-based random-effects pooled estimates for 5-year local control, eye retention, survival endpoint families, visual outcomes, and complications after radiotherapy for choroidal melanoma. The corrected comparative evidence is insufficient for a connected network meta-analysis. Manuscript claims should therefore describe pooled modality-specific outcomes and avoid causal treatment ranking unless a new source-traceable comparative dataset is built.

# Data Availability

The corrected extraction and analysis tables are available in the local project package:

- `05_extraction/extraction_study_characteristics.csv`
- `05_extraction/extraction_arm_extraction.csv`
- `05_extraction/extraction_outcomes_long.csv`
- `06_analysis/tables/analysis_ready_outcomes.csv`
- `07_manuscript/tables/`

# Why The Old v5 Manuscript/Analysis Is Wrong

Updated: 2026-04-27

## Bottom Line

The old v5 package is wrong because it was built from a small hand-curated
63-row reconstruction and hardcoded NMA inputs, not from the corrected
full-text screening, PDF QA, and extraction pipeline completed on 2026-04-27.

The old package can be internally arithmetic-consistent while still being
source-invalid.

## Root Causes

### 1. The old evidence base was not the corrected full-text set

Old layer:

- `02_data/studies_classified_choroidal.csv`: 63 rows
- After dropping helium: 60 rows
- Focused active radiotherapy rows: 57

Current corrected layer:

- `05_extraction/extraction_study_characteristics.csv`: 85 studies
- `05_extraction/extraction_arm_extraction.csv`: 128 arms
- `05_extraction/extraction_outcomes_long.csv`: 573 extracted outcome rows
- `06_analysis/tables/analysis_ready_outcomes.csv`: 218 analysis-ready rows

The old manuscript therefore describes a different evidence base.

### 2. The NMA input was hardcoded, not derived from extraction

The old scripts hardcode comparative NMA inputs:

- `03_analysis/code/09_final_5node_analysis.R`
- `09_green_journal_submission_v5_CLEAN/10_final_v5_bootstrap_audit.R`

Examples where old hardcoded values conflict with
`02_data/studies_classified_choroidal.csv`:

| Comparison arm | Hardcoded N/events | Old CSV N/LC/implied events | Problem |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Takiar I-125 | 214/198 | 156/92%/144 | denominator and events differ |
